note.explanation: An object's weight acts as if it is concentrated at one point called its centre of gravity. Its mass can also be treated as concentrated at one point called its centre of mass. In a uniform gravitational field, these points coincide. For an irregular plane lamina, suspend it from two different points and draw the vertical line each time; their intersection gives its centre of gravity.
examples: A rectangle's centre of gravity is at the intersection of its diagonals.
A cup's centre of gravity can lie outside the material of the cup.
note.checkAnswer: The point where the two vertical lines cross.
note.simple: Think of the centre of gravity as the point where an object's weight seems to act. For an irregular flat shape, hang it from two places: the crossing of the two vertical lines shows that point.
note.checkQuestion: When an irregular plane lamina is suspended from two different points, where is its centre of gravity?
note.title: Centre of Gravity and Centre of Mass
steps: Make a small hole near the edge of the lamina and suspend it freely from that point.
Hang a plumb line from the same point of suspension.
When the lamina stops moving, draw the vertical line along the plumb line.
Suspend the lamina from a different point and draw a second vertical line.
Mark the point where the two lines cross; this is the centre of gravity.
note.answer: For an irregular plane lamina, the centre of gravity is at the intersection of the vertical lines drawn when the lamina is suspended from different points.

options: The point where the body's total weight appears to act
The point where the body's speed is greatest
The point where the body touches the ground
The point where the body's volume is greatest
mcqs.stem: Which statement describes the centre of gravity of a body?
rationales: This is correct: the body's total weight appears to act at its centre of gravity.
This is incorrect because speed does not define the centre of gravity.
This is incorrect because the contact point with the ground need not be the centre of gravity.
This is incorrect because the centre of gravity is not defined by the body's volume.

options: The centre of the plate
The intersection of its diagonals
The intersection of its medians
One of its corners
mcqs.stem: Where is the centre of gravity of a uniform round plate?
rationales: This is correct: the centre of gravity of a round plate is at the centre of the plate.
This is incorrect because diagonals are used to locate the centre of a square or rectangle.
This is incorrect because the medians locate the centre of gravity of a triangle.
This is incorrect because a corner is not the geometrical centre of a round plate.

options: At the intersection of two vertical lines drawn from suspension points
At the lowest point of the lamina
At the point where the lamina is thickest
At the first point from which it was suspended
mcqs.stem: How can the centre of gravity of an irregular plane lamina be found experimentally?
rationales: This is correct: each vertical line passes through the centre of gravity, so their intersection locates it.
This is incorrect because the lowest point changes with the way the lamina is suspended.
This is incorrect because thickness does not determine the centre of gravity by this method.
This is incorrect because one suspension point gives only one vertical line, not the exact position.

options: It must always lie inside the material
It must always lie outside the material
It may lie inside or outside the material
It must always lie on the edge
mcqs.stem: Where may the centre of gravity of an object lie?
rationales: This is incorrect because the centre of gravity of a cup can lie outside its material.
This is incorrect because many solid, regular objects have their centre of gravity inside them.
This is correct: the centre of gravity may be inside a body or outside it.
This is incorrect because the centre of gravity does not have to be on the object's edge.

options: The whole mass of the body is assumed to be concentrated there
The whole weight of the body disappears there
The body has no acceleration there
The body must be supported there
mcqs.stem: What is meant by the centre of mass of a body?
rationales: This is correct: the centre of mass is the point where the body's whole mass is assumed to be concentrated.
This is incorrect because the body's weight does not disappear at the centre of mass.
This is incorrect because the definition of centre of mass does not mean acceleration is zero.
This is incorrect because a body need not be supported at its centre of mass.

options: They coincide
They are always at opposite ends
The centre of mass is always above the centre of gravity
They never coincide
mcqs.stem: On Earth's surface, where gravitational acceleration is almost uniform, how are the centre of mass and centre of gravity related?
rationales: This is correct: in an almost uniform gravitational field, the centre of mass coincides with the centre of gravity.
This is incorrect because the two points do not have to be at opposite ends.
This is incorrect because there is no general rule that one point is above the other.
This is incorrect because the textbook states that the two points coincide where g is almost uniform.

options: At the intersection of the diagonals
At the intersection of the medians
At the centre of the axis
At the centre of the sphere
mcqs.stem: Where is the centre of gravity of a uniform triangular lamina?
rationales: This is incorrect because the intersection of the diagonals gives the centre for a square or rectangle.
This is correct: the centre of gravity of a triangle is at the intersection of its medians.
This is incorrect because the centre of the axis is listed for a cylinder.
This is incorrect because the centre of a sphere is its centre of gravity.

options: It follows a straight-line path at constant speed
It moves in a circle because the wrench rotates
It remains fixed because there is no resultant force
It accelerates in the direction of the wrench's rotation
mcqs.stem: A rotating wrench slides along a frictionless floor with no resultant force on it. What does its centre of mass do?
rationales: This is correct: with no resultant force, the centre of mass follows a linear path with constant speed.
This is incorrect because the wrench's rotation does not make the centre of mass move in a circle.
This is incorrect because no resultant force does not mean the centre of mass must remain fixed.
This is incorrect because the wrench's rotation does not make its centre of mass accelerate.

written.text: Q4.8. Define centre of mass and centre of gravity of a body.
written.finalAnswer: The centre of mass is the point where the whole mass of the body is assumed to be concentrated. The centre of gravity is the point where the total weight of the body appears to be acting.

written.text: Q4.3. Discuss the concepts of stability and centre of gravity in relation to objects toppling over. Provide an example where an object’s centre of gravity affects its stability, and explain how altering its base of support can influence stability.
written.finalAnswer: An object is more likely to topple when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base of support. A higher centre of gravity makes toppling easier. For example, a tall narrow box is less stable than a short box. Widening the base of support makes the object more stable because the vertical line through its centre of gravity can move farther before falling outside the base.

For a question about a regular shape, learn the textbook's listed positions of the centre of gravity, such as the intersection of the diagonals of a rectangle.
Use the key idea that on Earth's surface, where g is almost uniform, the centre of mass and centre of gravity coincide.

explain.title: Centre of gravity
explain.body: Centre of gravity is that point where total weight of the body appears to be acting. If a body is supported at its centre of gravity, it stays there without rotation.

explain.title: Centre of mass
explain.body: The centre of mass of a body is that point where the whole mass of the body is assumed to be concentrated. It lets us describe the motion of a system as if its mass were concentrated at one point.

explain.title: Centres of regular shapes
explain.body: For the shapes listed in your textbook, the centre of gravity is at a geometrical position: for a square or rectangle it is where the diagonals intersect; for a triangle it is where the medians intersect.

explain.title: Finding the centre of gravity of an irregular lamina
explain.body: Each time an irregular plane lamina is suspended freely, its centre of gravity lies on the vertical line from the suspension point. Draw vertical lines for two different suspensions; their intersection gives the exact position. The centre of gravity may be inside or outside the body.

explain.title: Centre of mass and centre of gravity on Earth
explain.body: On the surface of the Earth, where g is almost uniform, the centre of mass of an object coincides with its centre of gravity.

mistakes: Do not swap the definitions: centre of mass is about the whole mass; centre of gravity is about the total weight.
Do not say the centre of gravity must always be inside the material; it can lie outside, as for a cup.
When describing the lamina experiment, do not stop after drawing just one line; use different suspension points and find where the lines cross.
Do not call the point of suspension the centre of gravity; it is the vertical line from that point that passes through the centre of gravity.
